e-491.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
e-491.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-492.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
e-492.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv'\,\textrm{d}x= uv- \int vu'\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle \int x \cos{2x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\int \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-6209.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
e-6209.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\int (-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+{\frac{1}{5}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{5}\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)]+[\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =[-\frac{\pi }{25}\cdot (-1)+0]+[0-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the integral ∫3xe−xdx.

b

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x and dv=e^{-x} dx gives v=-e^{-x}, so the integral is -3xe^{-x}+3∫e^{-x} dx=-3xe^{-x}-3e^{-x}+C. Differentiating confirms 3xe^{-x}.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate the integral ∫3xe−xdx.

a
2e−x−3xe−x+C
b
−3xe−x+e−x+C
c
3e−x−xe−x+C
d
−3xe−x−2e−x+C
e
−3xe−x−3e−x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xe−xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=e−x⟹v=−e−x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get ∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅e−xdx=3x⋅(−e−x)−∫(−e−x)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xe−xdx=−3xe−x+3∫e−xdx=−3xe−x−3e−x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{-x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x}\, & ⟹\,v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-x}+3\int {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-x}-3{e}^{-x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

∫3xe2x+5dx=

a
3e2x2−3xe2x4+C
b
3e2x+52−3xe2x+54+C
c
3xe2x+52−3e2x+54+C
d
xe2x+54+3e2x+54+C
e
e2x+52+3e2x+54+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=3x and dv=e^{2x+5} dx gives v=e^{2x+5}/2. Thus the integral is 3xe^{2x+5}/2−(3/2)∫e^{2x+5} dx=3xe^{2x+5}/2−3e^{2x+5}/4+C. Differentiation returns 3xe^{2x+5}.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xe2x+5dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=e2x+5⟹v=e2x+52.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅e2x+5dx=3x⋅e2x+52−∫e2x+52⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xe2x+5dx=3xe2x+52−32∫e2x+5dx=3xe2x+52−3e2x+54+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x{e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx.

a
−3xe−5x25−3e−5x25+C
b
−(3x+5)e5x5+3xe5x25+C
c
(3x+5)e−5x5+3xe−5x25+C
d
(3x+5)e−5x25−e−5x5+C
e
−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=3x+5 and dv=e^{-5x} dx gives v=-e^{-5x}/5. Thus the integral is −(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5+(3/5)∫e^{-5x} dx=−(3x+5)e^{-5x}/5−3e^{-5x}/25+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx.

a
−3xe−5x25−3e−5x25+C
b
−(3x+5)e5x5+3xe5x25+C
c
(3x+5)e−5x5+3xe−5x25+C
d
(3x+5)e−5x25−e−5x5+C
e
−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(3x+5)e−5xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x+5⟹u′=3v′=e−5x⟹v=−e−5x5.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(3x+5)⋅e−5xdx=(3x+5)⋅(−e−5x5)−∫(−e−5x5)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(3x+5)e−5xdx=−(3x+5)e−5x5+35∫e−5xdx=−(3x+5)e−5x5−3e−5x25+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+5\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-5x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x+5)\cdot {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x+5)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-5x}}{5})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x+5){e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}+\frac{3}{5}\int {e}^{-5x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x+5){e}^{-5x}}{5}-\frac{3{e}^{-5x}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

∫6xe4xdx=

a
xe4x3+xe4x9+C
b
3xe4x2−3e4x8+C
c
xe4x2−3e4x8+C
d
3xe4x2−3e4x9+C

e4x3+e4x9+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=6x and dv=e^{4x} dx gives v=e^{4x}/4. Therefore the integral is 3xe^{4x}/2−(3/2)∫e^{4x} dx=3xe^{4x}/2−3e^{4x}/8+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

∫6xe4xdx=

a
xe4x3+xe4x9+C
b
3xe4x2−3e4x8+C

xe4x2−3e4x8+C

3xe4x2−3e4x9+C

Submit

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫6xe4xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=6x⟹u′=6v′=e4x⟹v=14e4x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫6x⋅e4xdx=6x⋅14e4x−∫14e4x⋅6dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫6xe4xdx=32xe4x−32∫e4xdx=3xe4x2−3e4x8+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution gives 3xe^{4x}/2−3e^{4x}/8+C, exactly matching option b. Differentiating gives 6xe^{4x}, confirming the mathematics. The incorrect submission selected a.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{4x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}-\int \frac{1}{4}{e}^{4x}\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{4x}-\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3x{e}^{4x}}{2}-\frac{3{e}^{4x}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate the integral ∫(2x+1)e3xdx.

a
 (4x−1)e3x3+C
b
 (6x+4)e3x3+C
c
 (3x+2)e3x9+C
d
 (4x−3)e3x9+C
e
(6x+1)e3x9+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives (2x+1)e^{3x}/3−2e^{3x}/9+C=(6x+1)e^{3x}/9+C. Its derivative is (2x+1)e^{3x}, confirming option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (2x+1){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x+1\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (2x+1)\cdot {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =(2x+1)\cdot \frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}-\int \frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+1){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(2x+1){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(2x+1){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{2{e}^{3x}}{9}+C \\  & =\frac{(6x+1){e}^{3x}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Calculate the integral ∫(2x+1)e3xdx.

a
 (4x−1)e3x3+C
b
 (6x+4)e3x3+C
c
 (3x+2)e3x9+C
d
 (4x−3)e3x9+C
e
(6x+1)e3x9+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(2x+1)e3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x+1⟹u′=2v′=e3x⟹v=e3x3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(2x+1)⋅e3xdx=(2x+1)⋅e3x3−∫e3x3⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(2x+1)e3xdx=(2x+1)e3x3−23∫e3xdx=(2x+1)e3x3−2e3x9+C=(6x+1)e3x9+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (2x+1){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x+1\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{3x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (2x+1)\cdot {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =(2x+1)\cdot \frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}-\int \frac{{e}^{3x}}{3}\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+1){e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(2x+1){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\int {e}^{3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(2x+1){e}^{3x}}{3}-\frac{2{e}^{3x}}{9}+C \\  & =\frac{(6x+1){e}^{3x}}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x+3 and dv=cos(3x) dx gives v=sin(3x)/3. The integral is (x+3)sin(3x)/3−(1/3)∫sin(3x) dx=(x+3)sin(3x)/3+cos(3x)/9+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+3\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+3)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =(x+3)\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

∫(x+3)cos⁡(3x)dx=

a
−sin⁡(3x)3+xcos⁡(3x)9+C
b
(x+3)sin⁡(3x)3−xcos⁡(3x)3+C
c
(x+3)sin⁡(3x)3+cos⁡(3x)9+C
d
xsin⁡(3x)9+cos⁡(3x)3+C
e
(x+3)sin⁡(3x)9+cos⁡(3x)3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(x+3)cos⁡(3x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x+3⟹u′=1v′=cos⁡(3x)⟹v=sin⁡(3x)3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(x+3)⋅cos⁡(3x)dx=(x+3)⋅sin⁡(3x)3−∫sin⁡(3x)3⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(x+3)cos⁡(3x)dx=(x+3)sin⁡(3x)3−13∫sin⁡(3x)dx=(x+3)sin⁡(3x)3+cos⁡(3x)9+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+3\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+3)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =(x+3)\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x & =\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and dv=sin(2x) dx gives v=−cos(2x)/2. Thus the integral is −x cos(2x)+∫cos(2x) dx=−x cos(2x)+sin(2x)/2+C, matching option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

∫2xsin⁡(2x)dx=

a
−xcos⁡(2x)2+sin⁡(2x)4+C
b
cos⁡(4x)4+xsin⁡(4x)4+C
c
xcos⁡(2x)4+sin⁡(2x)2+C
d
−xcos⁡(2x)+sin⁡(2x)2+C
e
xcos⁡(2x)4−sin⁡(2x)4+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xsin⁡(2x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=sin⁡(2x)⟹v=−cos⁡(2x)2.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2x⋅sin⁡(2x)dx=2x⋅(−cos⁡(2x)2)−∫(−cos⁡(2x)2)⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xsin⁡(2x)dx=−xcos⁡(2x)+∫cos⁡(2x)dx=−xcos⁡(2x)+sin⁡(2x)2+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and dv=sin(x) dx gives v=−cos(x). Therefore the integral is −2x cos(x)+2∫cos(x) dx=−2x cos(x)+2sin(x)+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$

history.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=sin(3x+5) dx gives v=−cos(3x+5)/3. Thus the integral is −x cos(3x+5)/3+(1/3)∫cos(3x+5) dx=−x cos(3x+5)/3+sin(3x+5)/9+C, matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

b

c

d

e
cos⁡(3x+5)3+xsin⁡(3x+5)9+C

EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫xsin⁡(3x+5)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=sin⁡(3x+5)⟹v=−cos⁡(3x+5)3.

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅sin⁡(3x+5)dx=x⋅(−cos⁡(3x+5)3)−∫(−cos⁡(3x+5)3)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫xsin⁡(3x+5)dx=−xcos⁡(3x+5)3+13∫cos⁡(3x+5)dx=−xcos⁡(3x+5)3+sin⁡(3x+5)9+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x+5)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+5)}{9}+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 10
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
d
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
e
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=2x and dv=cos(4x) dx gives v=sin(4x)/4. Hence the integral is x sin(4x)/2−(1/2)∫sin(4x) dx=x sin(4x)/2+cos(4x)/8+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Calculate ∫2xcos⁡4xdx.

a
 3xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x4+C
b
 −sin⁡4x4+xcos⁡4x6+C
c
 xsin⁡4x4−cos⁡4x2+C
d
 −sin⁡4x8+xcos⁡4x2+C
e
 xsin⁡4x2+cos⁡4x8+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫2xcos⁡4xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=2x⟹u′=2v′=cos⁡4x⟹v=14sin⁡4x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫2xcos⁡4xdx=2x⋅14sin⁡4x−∫14sin⁡4x⋅2dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫2xcos⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12∫sin⁡4xdx=12xsin⁡4x−12(−14cos⁡4x)+C=12xsin⁡4x+18cos⁡4x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\int \frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-18x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=-18 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (-18x)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =(-18x)\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\cdot (-18)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}(-18x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}+6{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-6(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))-2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-6(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot 0-0\cdot 0)-2(-1-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives the antiderivative xe^{4x}/4−e^{4x}/16. At x=1/4 this is 0, and at x=0 it is −1/16. Therefore the integral is 1/16, option d.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{4x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{1/4}{e}^{4x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4}-{\frac{1}{16}{e}^{4x}|}_{0}^{1/4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{4(1/4)}-0\cdot {e}^{4\cdot 0}]-\frac{1}{16}[{e}^{4(1/4)}-{e}^{4\cdot 0}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\frac{e}{4}-0]-\frac{1}{16}[e-1] \\  & =\frac{e}{16}-\frac{e}{16}+\frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}3x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(2\cdot {e}^{4}-0\cdot {e}^{0})-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{4}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =3{e}^{4}-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{4}-1) \\  & =\frac{9{e}^{4}+3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

12π

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives −12x cos(x)+12sin(x). At π this equals 12π, and at −π it equals −12π. The integral is 24π, matching option e.

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=12x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=12 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 12x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =12x\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 12\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }12x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-12x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }+12{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-12x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }+12\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =-12[\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )] \\  & +12[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )] \\  & =-12[-\pi -\pi ]+12[0-0] \\  & =-12[-2\pi ] \\  & =24\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15

Evaluate ∫−ππ12xsin⁡(x)dx.

a
2π5
b
12π
c
23π12
d
36π
e
24π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's use integration by parts. We set u=12x⇒u′=12v′=sin⁡(x)⇒v=−cos⁡(x).

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫12x⋅sin⁡(x)dx=12x⋅(−cos⁡(x))−∫(−cos⁡(x))⋅12dx.

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

∫−ππ12xsin⁡(x)dx=−12xcos⁡(x)|−ππ+12∫−ππcos⁡(x)dx=−12xcos⁡(x)|−ππ+12sin⁡(x)|−ππ=−12[πcos⁡(π)+πcos⁡(−π)]=+12[sin⁡(π)−sin⁡(−π)]=−12[−π−π]+12[0−0]=−12[−2π]=24π.
